### The re-drive planner

Multi-thread effects become per-thread commands. `apps/server/src/loom/orchestration/redrive.ts`:

```ts
/** One episode-keyed command per affected thread. Pure over a graph snapshot. */
export const planReDrive = (rows: ReadonlyArray<LoomThreadWorkstream>): ReadonlyArray<OrchestrationV2ServerCommand> => [
  // cancel cascade: root cancelled → every live descendant with outcome null
  ...rows.filter((r) => r.outcome === "cancelled").flatMap((root) =>
    descendants(rows, root.threadId).filter((d) => d.outcome === null && d.deletedAt === null)
      .map((d) => outcomeSet(d.threadId, "cancelled", `server:loom:cascade-cancel:${root.outcomeEventId}:${d.threadId}`))),
  // wedged dependents: a live, unstarted node blocked on a cancelled same-parent sibling
  ...rows.filter((r) => r.outcome === null && r.kickoffAt === null && !r.attention.includes("needs_guidance"))
    .filter((r) => r.blockedBy.some((id) => cancelledSibling(rows, r, id)))
    .map((r) => attentionRaise(r.threadId, "needs_guidance", `server:loom:wedged:${cancelledDepEventId}:${r.threadId}`)),
  // archive / delete cascades keyed on the root's stamp; unarchive keyed on its event id
  ...rows.filter((r) => r.archivedAt !== null).flatMap((root) => descendants(rows, root.threadId)
    .filter((d) => d.archivedAt === null).map((d) => upstreamArchive(d.threadId, `server:loom:cascade-archive:${root.threadId}:${root.archivedAt}:${d.threadId}`))),
  ...rows.filter((r) => r.unarchivedEventId !== null && r.archivedAt === null).flatMap((root) => descendants(rows, root.threadId)
    .filter((d) => d.archivedAt !== null).map((d) => upstreamUnarchive(d.threadId, `server:loom:cascade-unarchive:${root.unarchivedEventId}:${d.threadId}`))),
  ...rows.filter((r) => r.deletedAt !== null).flatMap((root) => descendants(rows, root.threadId)
    .filter((d) => d.deletedAt === null).map((d) => upstreamDelete(d.threadId, `server:loom:cascade-delete:${root.threadId}:${root.deletedAt}:${d.threadId}`))),
  // goal attach down: a child with no goal whose parent has one
  ...rows.filter((r) => r.goalId === null && parentOf(rows, r)?.goalId).map((r) => goalSet(r.threadId, parentOf(rows, r)!.goalId, `server:loom:goal-attach:${r.threadId}:${parentOf(rows, r)!.goalId}`)),
  // gate legs from the latest route on a source (loop → rework on the target; loop-back → reverify on the source; resolve → resolve on the counterpart)
  ...rows.filter((r) => r.lastRoute !== null).map((r) => gateLegFor(r, rows)),
];
```

`runReDrivePass(orchestrator, commandReceipts, loomStore)` reads `listActiveWorkstreams()` (plus archived rows for the cascades), plans, skips any command whose id already has a receipt (`commandReceipts.getByCommandId`), dispatches the rest **sequentially** (one lock at a time, never nested), and classifies results: accepted → done; `LoomDispatchDeferredError` → leave for the next pass; any other error → log at warning with the episode key (the episode is receipted dead; Phase 3b's advisory rail surfaces it). The gate-leg text and `controlPayload` come from a `composeGateLeg` the dispatcher owns in 3b; Phase 2 ships it with a minimal fixed template so the test can run, marked for 3b to replace.

`LoomReDriveReactor` subscribes to `streamDomainEvents`, debounces on `thread.outcome-set | thread.route-taken | thread.archived | thread.unarchived | thread.deleted | thread.goal-set`, runs the pass, and runs once at startup. Phase 3b folds it into the dispatcher's pass (first rails, before promotion) and owns the periodic tick; until then the reactor is what keeps cascades and gates moving in the Phase 2 smoke.

The window the strategy accepted is visible here: between a reviewer's `route-taken` and the coder's `gate-rework-accepted` the board reads the coder as done for one pass; dependents cannot start in that window because `isMemberOfUnresolvedGate` (the reviewer is non-terminal and carries the loop route) already holds them, and the promotion predicate excludes gate members.

## 6. Quiescence as completion — the substrate half

The semantic: a started child that goes quiet without `workstream_submit` is treated as having yielded, not as owing a human. Phase 2 provides the state and the predicate; Phase 3b's rail writes the report and dispatches the synthesised submit.

- **The event and the state.** The dispatcher dispatches `thread.work.submit { threadId, reportPath, outcome: "quiescent" }` with a `server:loom:quiescent:<threadId>:<lastRunId>` id. The arm accepts `quiescent` only on `server:` ids, records `thread.outcome-recorded { outcome: "quiescent", decision: "yield", synthesised: true }` and raises `awaiting_orchestrator`. `routeWorkSubmit` returns `yield` for it before the rework interception (§2), so a gate member that goes quiet also yields and never resolves or loops its gate. Spawn and scaffold refuse `quiescent` in any route's `on` list.
- **The hook.** V2 run completion as projected: Phase 3b subscribes to `run.updated` with a terminal status on `streamDomainEvents` and re-evaluates on the periodic tick; it never listens to the adapter's `agent_settled`.
- **The predicate** (`apps/server/src/loom/orchestration/quiescence.ts`):

```ts
export const quiescenceCandidate = (input: {
  readonly shell: OrchestrationV2ThreadShell;        // joined: shell.workstream present
  readonly runs: ReadonlyArray<OrchestrationV2Run>;   // getThreadRecords(threadId, ["runs"]) for the few pre-filtered candidates
  readonly latestUserMessage: Pick<OrchestrationV2ConversationMessage, "createdBy" | "loom" | "createdAt"> | null;
  readonly children: ReadonlyArray<LoomThreadWorkstream>;
  readonly now: DateTime.Utc;
  readonly grace: { readonly controlStartedMs: number; readonly humanStartedMs: number | null }; // null = never for human-started turns
}): boolean => {
  const ws = input.shell.workstream;
  if (ws === undefined || ws.parentThreadId === null || ws.kickoffAt === null || ws.outcome !== null) return false;
  if (ws.attention.length > 0 || input.shell.pendingRuntimeRequest !== null) return false;
  if (input.shell.activityRunStatus !== null || input.runs.some((run) => run.status === "queued")) return false; // includes a held queue
  if (input.children.some((child) => child.outcome === null && child.deletedAt === null && child.archivedAt === null)) return false;
  const lastRun = latestUnheldRun(input.runs);
  if (lastRun?.completedAt == null) return false;
  const humanStarted = input.latestUserMessage?.createdBy === "user";
  const graceMs = humanStarted ? input.grace.humanStartedMs : input.grace.controlStartedMs;
  return graceMs !== null && DateTime.toEpochMillis(input.now) - DateTime.toEpochMillis(lastRun.completedAt) >= graceMs;
};
```

"Who started the last turn" is the latest user-role message's `createdBy` (a Loom control message is `agent`; the composer is `user`), cross-checked against the shell's `latestUserAuthoredMessageAt`. The grace values are settings owned by 3b; the defaults travel from the V1 idle backstop.

(6) *The goal rename is irreversible on a copied database* — it runs at first boot of the V2 server on `statev2.sqlite`; Phase 4's QA instance must boot a fresh copy, which it does by design.

content.text:
# Pull 9 Phase 2 — Loom's substrate on upstream's Orchestration V2

Loom is a Pi-first fork of `pingdotgg/t3code` whose product is an orchestration layer — goals, a shared task tree, a workstream graph of durable threads with roles, briefs, dependencies, review gates, attention flags, liveness and reports. Upstream's Orchestration V2 deleted the V1 engine that layer sat on, and the signed strategy (`plans/upstream-pull9-strategy/plan.mdx`, revision 3) decided to re-platform: `upstream/main` becomes the base and Loom's layer is re-expressed on it. Phase 1 (the mechanical merge, running in parallel) leaves V2 Loom booting with the workstream layer absent. **Phase 2 builds the seams that layer attaches to**: the sidecar contract beside upstream's closed unions, a Loom decider arm redesigned for V2's per-thread lock, the two dispatch/receipt-core hunks, the Loom projector and sidecar tables, the goal tables, the `1046+` migrations, and the substrate half of quiescence-as-completion. Phase 3's four tracks (MCP toolkit, dispatcher and rails, driver economics, web re-hang) consume what this plan delivers; Phase 4 imports Loom's historical data into the tables it defines.

**Done** means: the files below exist on the integration branch; `vp run typecheck` and `vp check` are green; the seven tests in *Verification* pass against V2's real orchestrator, event sink and SQL projection (no mocked engine); every hunk in an upstream file carries a `// loom:` marker and appears in the amended hunk inventory; and a Phase 3 coder can wire a tool handler or a dispatcher rail to the arm, the store and the shell join without making a design decision this plan left open.

<Callout tone="info">
**Authority.** Where this plan is silent, the strategy decides; where the strategy is silent, `consult_manager` with `author_doc` pointing at it before guessing. Decisions the strategy recorded (lane collapse, goals as plain tables, steer-when-steerable with tiers, quiescence adopted, no `delegate_task` for children, Loom data never on `AppThread`) are applied here, not re-opened. Every call this plan makes on its own is in the *Decision log* with the alternative rejected. Upstream code is cited at `upstream/main` `1a3f7ad508`; Loom's V1 code at `HEAD` `3cc6c015ab` is the behavioural spec being re-expressed.
</Callout>

## What Phase 1 leaves behind

Phase 2 coders start from the integration branch after Phase 1's runbook (`docs/upstream-sync/29-cadence-pull-9-phase1.md`) has run to its gate. Expect — and verify on day one, since the runbook's detach ledger (its Appendix C) is the authority:

- `apps/server/src/orchestration/` is gone. The 86 Loom files git relocated into `orchestration-v2/` sit under `quarantine/<original repo path>` at the repo root, excluded by three marked lines in the root `vite.config.ts`; nothing under `quarantine/` compiles. `packages/contracts/src/orchestration.loom.ts` (1,795 lines, imports the deleted V1 unions) and the `packages/shared` workstream libs (`workstreamGraph.ts`, `workstreamDependencies.ts`, `workstreamIsolation.ts`, `notify.ts`, `consultActivity.loom.ts`) are in quarantine too — Phase 2 retypes the first two and brings them back; the rest wait for their Phase 3 track.
- `apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/` is upstream's byte-for-byte (plus Phase 1's one sanctioned exception, the foreign-home guard re-seam). `Orchestrator.ts` has no Loom arm, `ProjectionStore.ts` no Loom fold, `packages/contracts/src/orchestrationV2.ts` no Loom splice.
- `apps/server/src/persistence/LoomMigrations.ts` carries `1001`–`1045` intact and `Sqlite.ts` still calls `runAllMigrations()`; the server boots on `statev2.sqlite`, copied once from `state.sqlite` by upstream's `initializeV2Database`. Migrations `1001`–`1045` have already run against the copy (their ledger rows travelled with it) and still run on a fresh install because upstream keeps the V1 schema migrations for its own lazy importer.
- `GoalId` / `GoalTaskId` remain in `packages/contracts/src/baseSchemas.ts` as a marked hunk. `apps/server/src/loom/serverLayers.ts` is split; every Loom reactor, sweep and worker is detached (not started). Upstream's recovery runs at its default `continueThreadsAfterServerUpdate = false`.
- Loom's web modules that read `LoomThreadShellFields` are excluded from the build (not stubbed). `settings.ts` carries upstream's `PiSettings` with two marked Loom hunks.

**Do not touch** in Phase 2: the MCP toolkit and tool handlers (`apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/workstream/`, Phase 3a); the dispatcher's rails beyond the re-drive planner this plan defines, liveness, exhaustion resume, the handoff drafter (3b); `PiAdapterV2.ts` / `PiRpc.ts` economics, the pi bump and patch regeneration (the strategy's Phase 2 driver items are planned separately — see *Scope and non-goals*); any `apps/web` or `apps/mobile` file (3d). Quarantined files are read as the behavioural spec and otherwise left alone until Phase 4 deletes them.

## The shape in one picture

<Mermaid
  caption="Where Loom attaches to V2. Solid: Phase 2. Dashed: the Phase 3 consumers that plug into the seams."
  source={"flowchart LR\n  subgraph upstream[Upstream V2 engine]\n    O[Orchestrator.ts dispatch switch]\n    DM[dispatchMessage]\n    DR[dispatchWithReceiptEffect]\n    ES[EventSink + EventStore]\n    PS[ProjectionStore.apply]\n    SH[getShellSnapshot / getThreadShell]\n  end\n  subgraph loom[Loom substrate - Phase 2]\n    C[orchestrationV2.loom.ts contract]\n    A[Orchestrator.loom.ts decider arm]\n    LP[loom/projection: applyLoomProjectionEvent + LoomStore + shell join]\n    RD[loom/orchestration/redrive.ts planner + reactor]\n    Q[loom/orchestration/quiescence.ts predicate]\n    LM[LoomMigrations 1046-1048 loom_* tables]\n  end\n  T3a[Phase 3a MCP toolkit handlers] -. Loom commands .-> O\n  T3b[Phase 3b dispatcher rails] -. control messages .-> O\n  T3b -. runs each pass .-> RD\n  T3b -. reads .-> Q\n  O -->|isLoomCommand| A\n  A -->|Loom events + nested upstream events| ES\n  ES --> PS\n  PS -->|isLoomDomainEvent| LP\n  DM -->|turn-start rules, start_if_idle, steer clause| A\n  DR -->|deferred pass-through, zero-event accept| A\n  SH -->|join workstream fields| LP\n  RD -->|idempotent per-thread commands| O\n  T3d[Phase 3d web] -. shell workstream fields and goal stream .-> SH\n"}
/>

Three facts about V2 decide the design, and each is checked against code rather than docs:

1. **One closed command/event union, one decider, one receipt per command id.** `OrchestrationV2DomainEvent` is a `Schema.Union` decoded straight from `orchestration_events.payload_json` (`persistence/Layers/OrchestrationEventStore.ts`, `decodeV2EventJson`), so a Loom event can only live in V2's log if it is a member of that union. `dispatchWithReceiptEffect` (`Orchestrator.ts:9690`) rejects any command producing no events and receipts every rejection; a repeated command id then returns `OrchestratorCommandPreviouslyRejectedError` forever.
2. **Per-thread lock, one projection per command.** `dispatchWithReceipt` runs under `threadDispatch.withLock(commandThreadId(command))` (`Orchestrator.ts:9878`); the keyed executor is neither re-entrant nor deadlock-aware; upstream nests into another thread only when it has just created it (`dispatchDelegatedTaskRequest` writes child events under the parent lock) and otherwise takes locks *sequentially, never nested* (`handleTerminalRun`, `:9883`).
3. **Delivery modes are fixed and a notification is only legal on `queue_after_active`.** `message.dispatch` offers `defer_start | steer_active | restart_active | queue_after_active | start_immediately` (`orchestrationV2.ts:2735`); a `notification` on anything but a server/provider-created `queue_after_active` is a receipted rejection (`Orchestrator.ts:4517–4528`); queuing happens only when a blocking run exists (`shouldQueue`, `:4696`); the delegated-completion block converts a queued wake to a steer when the target is `running` with a running provider turn on a session that supports active steering without interrupting tools (`:4570–4605`).

## Files

    { path: "packages/shared/src/workstreamGraph.ts", change: "modified", note: "Out of quarantine, retyped on outcome/held/kickoffAt (planLane gone); routeWorkSubmit gains the reserved quiescent outcome; isolation/fan-in predicates removed." },

content.text:
`awaiting_approval` / `awaiting_input` are **not** stored and not joined: they are `shell.pendingRuntimeRequest.kind` read at the consumer. Brief-needed attention on a parent is a dispatcher/board computation (Phase 3b/3d) over the children's `kickoffBriefPath`. The board's columns are derived, never stored: *held* = `held`; *blocked* = not held, some `blockedBy` outcome not `done`; *ready* = not held, deps done, `kickoffAt` null; *in progress* = `kickoffAt` set, `outcome` null; *done*; *cancelled*. `awaiting_orchestrator` is an attention reason, not a column.

### Enums and small types

```ts
export const LoomAttentionReason = Schema.Literals(["error", "awaiting_acceptance", "needs_guidance", "awaiting_orchestrator"]);
export const LoomOutcome = Schema.Literals(["done", "cancelled"]);               // stored as NullOr
export const LoomMessageOrigin = Schema.Literals(["kickoff", "orchestrator", "control_notice", "notify"]); // absent = not Loom-originated
export const LoomMessageFields = Schema.Struct({ origin: LoomMessageOrigin, controlPayload: Schema.optional(ControlPayload) });
export const WorkstreamRoute = Schema.Struct({ on: Schema.Array(TrimmedNonEmptyString), kind: Schema.Literals(["loop", "resolve"]), to: Schema.optional(ThreadId), maxRounds: Schema.optional(PositiveInt) });
export const WorkOutcomeDecision = Schema.Literals(["terminal", "attention", "loop", "resolve", "cap-breach", "yield"]);
export const RESERVED_OUTCOMES = ["quiescent"] as const; // refused in any route's `on`; accepted only on server: ids
export const DEFAULT_GATE_MAX_ROUNDS = 2; export const MAX_GATE_MAX_ROUNDS = 10;
```

`ControlPayload`, `ControlPayloadItem`, `WorkOutcomeCounts`, `HandoffDestination`, `NotifySendLogEntry`, `LoomThreadConsultSummary`, `LoomThreadPeerMessageSummary`, `LoomGoal`, `LoomGoalTask` (recursive `children`), `LoomGoalShell` move from the quarantined file with their shapes unchanged (rename `Orchestration*` to `Loom*`).

### Commands — extended beside upstream's union

Every Loom command is a `Schema.Struct` with `type`, `commandId`, `threadId` (the lock key — see §2) and `createdAt: IsoDateTime`. The members are exported as two tuples and spliced at the **HEAD** of upstream's unions with one marked line each, exactly the V1 pattern: client-dispatchable ones into `OrchestrationV2Command` (so the existing `orchestration.dispatchCommand` ws method and the MCP layer's `stableCommandId` carry them with no new transport), server-only ones into `OrchestrationV2InternalCommand`.

<Table
  columns={["Command", "Union", "Lock thread (commandThreadId)", "Fields beyond type/commandId/threadId/createdAt"]}
  rows={[
    ["thread.spawn", "internal", "parentThreadId ?? threadId", "parentThreadId: NullOr(ThreadId), projectId, title, modelSelection, runtimeMode, interactionMode, branch, worktreePath, role, purpose, goalId: NullOr(GoalId), anchorTaskId?, kickoffBriefPath?, blockedBy?, routes?, held?, spawnGeneration?, forkFromThreadId?, continuesThreadId?, graphKey?, createdBy, creationSource"],
    ["thread.scaffold", "internal", "parentThreadId (threadId = parentThreadId)", "held?, nodes: Array of {threadId, graphKey, role, title, purpose, blockedBy?, routes?, held?, spawnGeneration?, forkFromThreadId?, anchorTaskId?, modelSelection}"],
    ["thread.goal.set", "client", "threadId", "goalId: NullOr(GoalId), anchorTaskId?: NullOr(GoalTaskId)"],
    ["thread.held.set", "client", "threadId", "held: Boolean"],
    ["thread.outcome.set", "client", "threadId", "outcome: NullOr(LoomOutcome)"],
    ["thread.attention.raise", "client", "threadId", "reason: LoomAttentionReason"],
    ["thread.attention.clear", "client", "threadId", "reason?: LoomAttentionReason (absent = clear all stored)"],
    ["thread.dependencies.set", "client", "threadId", "blockedBy: Array(ThreadId)"],
    ["thread.kickoff-brief.set", "internal", "threadId", "kickoffBriefPath"],
    ["thread.work.submit", "internal", "threadId", "reportPath, outcome?, contested?, counts?"],
    ["thread.gate.rework", "internal", "threadId (the coder)", "sourceThreadId, round, routeEventId, message: {messageId, text, controlPayload}"],
    ["thread.gate.reverify", "internal", "threadId (the reviewer)", "sourceThreadId, round, routeEventId, message: {messageId, text, controlPayload}"],
    ["thread.gate.resolve", "internal", "threadId (the counterpart)", "sourceThreadId, routeEventId"],
    ["thread.consult.record", "internal", "threadId (asker)", "targetThreadId, targetTitle, question, answer, resolved, durationMs, forkSessionPath?"],
    ["thread.peer-message.record / .mark-delivered / .expire", "internal", "threadId (sender)", "as V1: recordId, targetThreadId, targetTitle, message, framedMessage"],
    ["thread.handoff.record", "internal", "threadId", "drafterThreadId, destinationGoalId, destinationThreadId"],
  ]}
/>

Not carried from V1: `thread.plan-lane.set` (becomes `held.set` + `outcome.set`), `thread.fanin.set` (shared checkout only), `thread.user-input.dismiss` (upstream has it under the same name and accepts message-capability requests), `goal.*` (goals are plain tables written by handlers), `thread.turn-start.fail` and `thread.stuck-launch.recover` (pending the strategy's stuck-launch verification in the driver work item; added later only if that verification keeps them). There is **no kickoff command**: the kickoff is a `message.dispatch` carrying `loom.origin: "kickoff"` (§3), and `kickoffAt` is stamped by the `dispatchMessage` hunk on any first turn.

### Events — extended beside upstream's union

A factory over upstream's non-exported `OrchestrationV2EventBase.fields` (the V1 `makeLoomOrchestrationEventMembers` pattern), spliced at the HEAD of `OrchestrationV2DomainEvent`. Every Loom event has `threadId` = the sidecar row it changes.

<Table
  columns={["Event", "Payload", "Projector effect on loom_thread_workstream"]}
  rows={[
    ["thread.workstream-created", "the initial record: parentThreadId, rootThreadId, projectId, goalId, anchorTaskId, role, purpose, graphKey, kickoffBriefPath, held, blockedBy, routes, spawnGeneration, forkFromThreadId, continuesThreadId", "INSERT (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING — replay-safe)"],
    ["thread.goal-set", "goalId, anchorTaskId?", "UPSERT goal_id/anchor_task_id, creating the row for a goal-less root"],
    ["thread.held-set", "held", "held, held_since"],

    ["thread.dependencies-set", "blockedBy", "blocked_by, dependencies_since"],

    ["thread.gate-warning", "kind: reopened-with-started-dependents | target-done-mid-round, detail, threadIds", "none (Phase 3b surfaces it to the parent)"],
    ["thread.consult-recorded", "as V1", "INSERT loom_thread_consults"],

# Phase 2 substrate plan — delivered

**Plan:** `/home/Carl/.t3/cockpit/worktrees/loom/t3code-87358b97/plans/upstream-pull9-phase2-substrate/plan.mdx` — signed (`plan`), render gate clean (`lint-plan.mjs` OK; rendered page beside it), committed `77f01f71ea` on `t3code/plan-next-upstream-merge` with only the plan staged. It is written for a coder who needs no further design decisions: every seam has its file, type/function signature or SQL, the hunk it needs in upstream and the test that proves it. Phase 3's four tracks and Phase 4's importer can be planned against its named seams (`LoomStoreV2` methods, the Loom command/event unions, `start_if_idle`, `LoomDispatchDeferredError`, `planReDrive`, `quiescenceCandidate`, `LoomGoalBroadcast`, `isEligibleToStart`).

## The four most consequential choices

1. **Loom commands and events are spliced into upstream's closed unions (HEAD position, V1's pattern), not kept in a parallel table.** Verified against code: V2 decodes `orchestration_events.payload_json` through `OrchestrationV2DomainEvent` and commits events + receipt + projection in one transaction; a sidecar sink could share none of that. The widened union surfaces every exhaustive switch (five known sites listed) — each gets a marked Loom branch.
2. **Cascades are state-derived re-drive, not decider hunks.** Subtree archive/unarchive/delete and cancel cascades, wedged-dependent raises, goal-attach-down and gate legs are produced by a pure `planReDrive(graph)` as episode-keyed idempotent per-thread commands (`server:loom:<kind>:<episodeEventId>:<target>`), run one lock at a time; goal archive/unarchive/rename cascades are *projector folds* of upstream's own thread events into `loom_goals`. This **removes four hunks from the strategy's inventory** (`thread.archive|unarchive|delete`, `thread.metadata.update`) and adds the mechanical ones (lock key, guard arm, four message-field carries, shell join, one new service in two `storesLayer`s). The inventory amendment table is in the plan.
3. **`kickoffAt` is stamped by the `dispatchMessage` hunk on any first turn — there is no kickoff command.** The kickoff is a `message.dispatch` with `loom.origin: "kickoff"`; a human-started first turn also counts as started, which the promotion rule needs. The deferral (`start_if_idle` → `LoomDispatchDeferredError`, no receipt) is confined to exactly two raise sites (busy FYI target; a gate leg behind a pending merge-back); everything permanently unsatisfiable is rejected once — the reviewer's note applied.
4. **Goal, task, consult and peer-message tables are renamed in place (migrations 1047/1048), not imported.** Upstream's legacy importer preserves thread ids and the V1 schemas are already right, so goal history arrives with zero import code. **Phase 4's planner (f939a37c) must know this**: its importer shrinks to `projection_threads` → `loom_thread_workstream` plus the session binding; the plan's §5 lists the one-to-one column mapping for the six-lane collapse and the kickoff rule.

## Decision log (18 entries in the plan; the ones the parent should know)

- Projector runs inside `ProjectionStore.apply` with the sink's `SqlClient` (read-your-writes for handlers); `LoomStoreV2` is a separate read/write service.
- `makeLoomChildThread` uses an explicit field list (no parent spread — the spread leaks pin/order/limitRecovery/rollback state); `forkedFrom: null` is load-bearing: it is what keeps `finalizeAppOwnedSubagent` and the `task_status` wake away from Loom children.
- Spawn/scaffold lock the **parent** (upstream's `dispatchDelegatedTaskRequest` precedent) so concurrent spawns under one parent serialise.
- `loom {origin, controlPayload}` lives on `ConversationMessage` only (web resolves by messageId).
- Upstream's un-settle-on-any-dispatch is accepted; the finished-root prompt settle is a `ThreadSettlementService` hunk.
- A human's first message to a *held* node clears `held`; a control message to a held node is refused.
- Supersede is specified (slot + predicate) but implemented in 3a with `runtime-request.create`.
- Metric columns (cost/context/diffs) leave the sidecar; `brief` string dies in favour of `kickoffBriefPath` only; isolation/fan-in columns are not created.
- `held` stays (strategy's recorded decision); its retirement is a listed three-line deletion.
- Phase 2 ships a ~40-line `LoomReDriveReactor` (event-triggered + startup) that 3b absorbs into the dispatcher pass — one of the two open questions.

## What I could not settle from the strategy and upstream's code (the plan's bottom form)

1. Whether a `notify_thread` peer message should clear the target's stored attention when it starts/steers the target (the strategy's "any Loom origin clears" rule says yes; it can erase a child's `awaiting_acceptance` on a sibling's FYI). Recommended: follow the strategy.
2. Whether the re-drive reactor ships in Phase 2 or only the planner/runner (recommended: ship it).

## Scope boundary the parent must act on

The strategy's Phase 2 also lists **driver-side items** — bundled patched pi, open-session fields → argv, patch 0001 → RPC `switch_session`, pi 1.0.2 bump, `costUsd` on usage, the stuck-launch verification, the Pi-default-sentinel and provider-binding doctrine checks. <addendum>
You operate inside T3 Code's work model: Goals → Tasks → Workstream. This is how every thread here is organised, whatever its role.

A GOAL is a single durable objective that outlives any one session and spans many — the north star for all work under it. Orient to it; if work drifts from the goal, refocus or update it. A goal is decomposed into a TASK TREE: the living, shared record of what is done and what remains — for the agents working it and for the human who glances at it to re-orient. It is kept current as work progresses.

Work happens in a WORKSTREAM: a tree of durable threads. You are one thread in it, and your role overlay says how you act within it. A ROOT thread ORCHESTRATES — it plans, delegates, and reviews rather than doing the work by hand. A CHILD thread EXECUTES a single self-contained brief and hands a result back. A child is a real, persistent thread a human can open and talk to, not a throwaway: spawning one is deliberate, and a child starts fresh — it inherits none of the parent's conversation, only the brief it is given. Work flows down as briefs and back up as reports. The workstream is a graph of threads: dependencies are its edges, so dependent work waits while independent branches run in parallel (with bounded review-gate loops as the one deliberate cycle) — and the graph is not fixed; it is expected to be amended and replanned as understanding improves.

Getting information from another thread, cheapest first: a thread's REPORT is its curated hand-back — read that first. The workstream GRAPH lets you see every thread and find any of them without searching (`workstream_list`). To resolve an ambiguity, CONSULT the thread that holds the context. The full thread history can be accessed via the Pi session jsonl file if necessary.

A few principles keep this coherent:
- Your assignment is your task. For a child that is its spawn brief; at the root it is the user's direction. An inherited goal is background - align to it, but where it and your assignment differ, follow the assignment.
- Work at your level, and keep heavy sub-phases out of your context. If you orchestrate, delegate substantial work to children rather than absorbing it inline, and when new non-trivial work crystallises mid-conversation, pause to lay out or amend the graph before diving in. If you execute a brief, do it yourself rather than re-delegating it — but any thread, at any depth, may hand a bounded sub-phase of its own brief to a child when all three hold: the sub-phase is context-heavy; a short brief can carry everything it needs from you; and what comes back is an artefact — files on disk plus a short report — not understanding you must carry into later turns. Typical cases: a screenshot-capture pass, a large-corpus read, a bulk extraction. Done in situ, every page of that stays in your context for the rest of the thread; done by a child, it dies with the child. It is a trade, not a reflex: a child starts cold, so you pay to write the brief and to wait for it — a sub-phase of a few turns is cheaper inline. Where the delegation tools are dormant for your role, `enable_toolset` activates them.
- Status describes the plan; runtime is the truth. A thread's status is where it sits in the workflow; whether its agent is actually working is a separate, system-tracked fact. Lean on the system's signals for a child's state rather than inferring from a single quiet look — and if a signal looks wrong for what you can plainly see, verify rather than act blindly.
- System notices are not the human. Automated workstream notices (a child finished, needs attention, recovered) are control-plane signals for you to act on, not messages from the user.
- Your worktree is your workspace. Every edit and commit you make lands in your own worktree (your process cwd) and nowhere else — any other checkout of this project (another thread's worktree, the parent's worktree, or the project's base workspace root) is read-only context (reports, evidence), never somewhere to `cd` into and write. This matters doubly if you orchestrate: children's worktrees are cut from YOUR branch, so a file committed anywhere else — however canonical its path looks — is invisible to every child you spawn. If a brief seems to require editing outside your own worktree, that is a brief error: surface it rather than comply.
- File references in replies and reports: use the full absolute path in inline code, one span per file or directory. Do not use bare basenames, paths relative to a shell `cd`, or fenced blocks for these references. The client resolves relative paths from the thread's worktree root, not the cwd inside a bash command.
- Search your worktree, not the roots above it. Your worktree is small, but the workspace and cockpit roots that contain it are vast (every sibling worktree's node_modules), so an unbounded `find`/`grep` from one of those roots can crawl for many minutes. Never search them unscoped: stay within your worktree, or bound the walk (`-maxdepth`, a named subtree, or a tool like `rg` that skips gitignored trees) rather than let a search wander into other threads' trees. A guard blocks unbounded recursive searches outside your worktree and auto-bounds unbounded search pipelines to 30s — when a file is not where you expected, do not search wider: verify the exact paths your brief gave you first (brief paths are authoritative), then run a focused bounded search, and only as a last resort consult the thread that holds the context (`consult_thread` — expensive).
- Setup may still be running. Worktree environment setup can run in the background after you start, so before any command that needs the project environment (installs, builds, tests, typecheck, dev servers) check the setup breadcrumb — `cat "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)/t3code-setup-state.json"`: `ready` proceed; `pending` do reading/editing/planning first and re-check (poll, don't run installs yourself); `failed` inspect its `detail` and the setup terminal output, then fix or report the setup failure rather than blindly rerunning installs; file absent means no setup script was configured — assume the repo is in its normal provided state.

You are thread `acf16362-ab78-48e8-ba7b-330f3b4436b8` in this workstream: the id every workstream tool takes, the id the human sees, and the id you quote when reporting. Your own conversation history is the pi session jsonl at `$PI_SESSION_FILE` (set in every shell command you run), a file named `*_acf16362-ab78-48e8-ba7b-330f3b4436b8.jsonl`. To reach ANOTHER thread's history, use its report or `consult_thread`; its jsonl is not necessarily in the same directory as yours.

You are a planner sub-thread. Produce intent briefs and implementation plans — the thinking, not the code.

- Your spawn brief defines your assignment — the plan you owe, not a script. If you discover the brief rests on a wrong assumption, or planning surfaces something material it didn't anticipate, surface it (in the plan's risks, or via `needs_guidance` if it invalidates the brief) rather than silently re-scoping.
- Your deliverable is a plan, not an implementation. Investigate the codebase as deeply as needed, but do not write feature code — decisions and their rationale are what you hand back.

- A good plan states intent, decomposition into work items, contracts and risks, and acceptance criteria — enough that its correctness can be judged before implementation.
- Write for a reader with none of your context. The coder threads that implement the plan inherit nothing you've read or reasoned through; the plan must stand alone.

Tasks outside your branch are read-only — say what needs doing there in your report. Record actionable work your planning surfaces with `goal_task_add` under the phase it belongs to. Your plan's decomposition is not yours to impose on the rest of the tree: hand that intended shape back in your report, along with details, findings and verdicts.

Raise it only when work genuinely must wait; a plan no human has to see first just completes.

# Phase 2 substrate plan review: needs rework (8 must-fix, 12 nice-to-have)

**Reviewed:** `/home/Carl/.t3/cockpit/worktrees/loom/t3code-87358b97/plans/upstream-pull9-phase2-substrate/plan.mdx` at `77f01f71ea`, against `upstream/main` (`1604ccc9d7`; it differs from the plan's `1a3f7ad508` by one commit, which does not touch `orchestration-v2/` or `contracts`). Upstream line references are at `upstream/main`.

**Verdict.** The architecture holds up, and the four consequential choices rest on true code facts. The problems are local:
- several hunks are attached to a seam that does not exist where the plan says it does;
- one cascade can never fire;
- the goal broadcast would be dropped by the client;
- the plan does not yet reflect orchestrator ruling 1.

Every fix is a paragraph or a sentence. None reopens a design choice. Ruling 2 (the re-drive reactor ships in Phase 2) is already reflected (D16, the file tree, §4).

## Verified true (no action)

- **(a) Splicing into upstream's unions is necessary.**
  - Events are decoded from `payload_json` through the union (`persistence/Layers/OrchestrationEventStore.ts:89,114`).
  - `EventSink.commitCommand` writes the receipt, the events, the projection and the outbox in one `sql.withTransaction` (`EventSink.ts:517–568`, `:239–261`).
- **(b) Spawn locking the parent has upstream precedent.** `commandThreadId` returns `parentThreadId` for `delegated_task.*` and `thread.created.record` (`Orchestrator.ts:415–420`), and the comment at `:9883–9888` documents the sequential, non-nested lock discipline.
- **(c) `forkedFrom: null` keeps upstream's delegated-task machinery away from Loom children.** Both `appOwnedSubagentParentThreadId` and `finalizeAppOwnedSubagent` require `forkedFrom.type === "node"` (`Orchestrator.ts:8622–8631`, `:8882–8888`).
- **(d) The importer preserves thread ids.** `importedThread` sets `id: ThreadId.make(row.thread_id)` (`legacy/LegacyV1ThreadImporter.ts:190`). The V1 goal schema (`1003_GoalsAndTasks.ts`) matches the `LoomGoal` and `LoomGoalTask` models.
- **(e) A deferred error can skip the receipt.** `Effect.catch` before `commitRejectedCommand` is the right place (`Orchestrator.ts:9765–9797`). The zero-event accepted-receipt path exists (`:9799–9822`). Note that `commitCommand` dies on zero events (`EventSink.ts:542`), which is why the plan's routing through the existing branch is correct.
- **(f) A Loom projector can run inside the commit.** `ProjectionStore.apply` has `sql` in scope and is called inside the commit transaction (`ProjectionStore.ts:1679`, `EventSink.ts:333`). Its trailing `updatedAt` bump (`:2513–2552`) behaves as D14 describes.
- **Also verified:**
  - the four message construction sites (`:3765`, `:4874`, `:5217`, `:5909`);
  - the notification rule (`:4588–4599`);
  - `shouldQueue` and the merge-back rejection (`:4697–4709`);
  - the delegated steer block;
  - the data model matches the 1046 SQL column for column;
  - `lint-plan.mjs` reports "OK — no findings".

## Must-fix

### M1. Ruling 1 is not reflected: `notify` and other Loom origins still clear attention

The plan says the opposite of the ruling in three places:
- turn-start rule 4 clears attention when `command.createdBy === "user" || command.loom?.origin !== undefined`;
- the open-question form still recommends "clear";
- `thread.outcome.set` clears attention only when the new outcome is terminal.

**Correction:**
- **Rule 4** clears only when `command.createdBy === "user" || command.loom?.origin === "orchestrator"` (that is, `workstream_prompt`). `kickoff`, `control_notice` (gate legs, wakes, digests) and `notify` clear nothing.
- **Outcome writes clear attention.** Every outcome write (`thread.outcome.set` to any value including `null`, terminal `work.submit`, `gate.resolve`) emits `attention-cleared`.
- **Remove the `QuestionForm`.** Both of its questions are now ruled.
- **State the consequences**, so the 3a and 3b planners and coders build on them:
  - a stored hold now survives `notify` turns and control-notice turns;
  - `holdErasedByCompletion` (`packages/shared/src/workstreamGraph.ts:448`) is keyed on *standing* attention, not attention raised this turn, so a child whose earlier hold survived a notify turn will have its completing submit refused. That is intended ("holds hold"). The `workstream_submit` description's "you raised this turn" wording changes meaning, so 3a should rewrite it;
  - the steered-tier wakes and gate legs in §3 no longer clear the target's hold.
- **Tests:** add a case to `t-quiescence` or a new test: a `notify`-origin message to a child holding `awaiting_acceptance` leaves it standing; `origin: "orchestrator"` clears it.

### M2. The one shared seam with the driver plan, the open-session field, is not specified

The plan says the driver items "share nothing … except the `loom` open-session field" (line 82) and never defines that field. There is no shape, no location and no owner. Upstream's `ProviderAdapterV2OpenSessionInput` is a server-side type, used for example at `Adapters/ClaudeAdapterV2.ts:2988`.

**Correction:** add a short subsection that pins down:
- the field's shape, per strategy Area G: `loom?: { appendSystemPrompt, skills, extensions }` on `ProviderAdapterV2OpenSessionInput`, plus how the `forkFrom` identity is carried;
- that the field and the `ProviderSessionManager` composition hook belong to the driver plan;
- which substrate reads the hook consumes: `LoomStoreV2.getWorkstream` (role, goalId, anchorTaskId, forkFromThreadId, continuesThreadId), `goals.get` and `tasks.listByGoal`;
- that the substrate adds nothing else for it.

With that, the driver plan can be written independently.

### M3. The restart-recovery hook point does not exist, and the kickoff re-delivery row contradicts the plan's own design

The plan places "one marked call into `loomRecoveryPolicy` after reconciliation, before continuation". Upstream has no such moment:
- `reconcileProjection` commits the reconciliation events **and** the `provider-runtime.continue` effect in one `commitCommand` (`ProviderRuntimeRecoveryService.ts:642–653`, `:680–690`), with `enabled` decided per thread before the call (`:741–745`);
- `prepareForShutdown` separately enqueues a continuation effect at graceful shutdown for every continuable thread (`:767–795`).

A post-reconcile call therefore cannot stop a flagged or cancelled thread from being continued. Separately, the row "kickoffAt set but no run ever started … re-delivered verbatim by the dispatcher's receipt-keyed kickoff" cannot happen under this plan: rule 5 stamps `kickoffAt` when the kickoff is accepted, and the kickoff's `message.dispatch` already holds an accepted receipt. So neither promotion nor a receipt-keyed re-send fires.

**Correction:**
- **Pick a real seam for "not continued".** Two work:
  - gate `enabled` per thread before `reconcileProjection` and inside `prepareForShutdown`;
  - or veto inside the `dispatchMessage` hunk when `command.restartContinuationOfRunId !== undefined`. `RestartContinuation.ts:156–172` dispatches through `message.dispatch`, and upstream already accepts a stale continuation as a no-op `thread.metadata-updated` (`Orchestrator.ts:~4385–4408`).
- **Say where the held-queue release runs.**
- **Rewrite the kickoff row** to say what actually re-delivers a cut kickoff, or that quiescence surfaces it to the parent instead.

### M4. The finished-root settle hunk reads a field the settlement path never has

The hunk reads `thread.workstream?.outcome` in `resolveAutoSettlementAt`. But that function receives a `ProjectionSettlementCandidate` (`ProjectionStore.ts:166–191`), which `ThreadSettlementService` loads from `projections.getSettlementCandidates` (`ThreadSettlementService.ts:278`), not from the joined `getShellSnapshot`. The plan's claim that "every consumer — ws, MCP, settlement, PR services — reads the joined shape" is therefore false for settlement. The sketch also dereferences `thread.workstream.parentThreadId` when `workstream` is `undefined` (`undefined !== null` is true).

**Correction:** have the settlement hunk read `LoomStoreV2` itself, for example through `ThreadSettlementService.make` with `LoomStore.layer` added to its layer. Fix the predicate to `ws !== null && ws.outcome !== null && ws.parentThreadId === null`.

### M5. The delete cascade can never fire

`runReDrivePass` reads "`listActiveWorkstreams()` (plus archived rows for the cascades)". `listActiveWorkstreams` excludes deleted rows, so `rows.filter((r) => r.deletedAt !== null)` is always empty. Upstream's `thread.delete` does not cascade to lineage children (`ThreadDeletion.ts` only handles `subagents` rows), so deleting a Loom root would leave its children live, hidden from the sidebar, and possibly still running.

**Correction:** specify the planner's input precisely: live rows, plus cancelled, archived and deleted *roots that still have a non-terminal or unarchived descendant*. A `LoomStoreV2` query does this naturally. Add a delete case to `t-lock`.

### M6. The goal broadcast's sequence makes the client drop every goal item

§4 says goal items carry `sequence = latestApplicationSequence`, "so the client's cursor logic keys it like any other shell item". Upstream's client applies a delta only when `item.sequence > snapshot.snapshotSequence` (`packages/client-runtime/src/state/shell.ts`, the `applyItems` branch). A goal write emits no thread event, so its sequence equals the sequence the client already holds, and the item is dropped. If 3d's handler did advance `snapshotSequence` on an item merged from a separate PubSub, it could skip thread deltas that have not yet arrived.

**Correction:** carry goal changes in a form the cursor does not gate. Upstream's own precedent is that enrichment refreshes are emitted as `kind: "snapshot"` items (`ws.ts:~1044–1070`, `ShellStream.ts` `shellStreamItemFromEnrichmentRefresh`). Alternatives are a dedicated Loom subscription, or a documented 3d bypass. State the contract 3d builds on.

### M7. False claim: `startNextQueuedRun` does not call `dispatchMessage`

The plan says "the `message.dispatch` case, PR-watch sync, `runtime-request.respond`, delegated dispatch and `startNextQueuedRun` call it directly — which is why the turn-start rules live there and nowhere else". `dispatchMessage` has four callers: `:2292`, `:6532`, `:7006` and `:9556`. `startNextQueuedRun` (`:1210`) writes the queued run's start and its `provider-turn.start` effect directly (`:1806–1811`). The turn-start rules therefore run when a message is *accepted* (queued), not when it starts.

Concrete case: a human message queued behind a running turn clears attention at queue time. If the agent then raises `awaiting_acceptance` at the end of that turn, the human's message starts with the hold standing, and the agent's completing submit is refused.

**Correction:** fix the sentence and state the acceptance-time semantics as intended, or add a marked hunk in `startNextQueuedRun` for user-authored queued messages. Either way the rationale paragraph must be true.

### M8. §5's Phase 4 import account is incomplete

Two of §5's statements do not hold, and one strategy rule is missing.

1. **Imported children have no V2 lineage.** Upstream's importer writes every imported thread with `lineage: { parentThreadId: null, relationshipToParent: null, rootThreadId: threadId }` (`LegacyV1ThreadImporter.ts:222–226`). Imported Loom children would therefore appear as top-level sidebar threads and receive thread notifications. "Phase 4's importer shrinks to the sidecar and session binding" omits this. I added task `f78944f6` under the Phase 4 import plan.
2. **"No Loom event exists for them and no episode-keyed rail fires" no longer holds**, because D3 made the cascades derived from stored state. On the first pass after import, imported rows with `outcome_event_id NULL` would trigger:
   - the cancel cascade, with id `server:loom:cascade-cancel:null:<d>`;
   - the wedged-dependent raise of `needs_guidance` on every abandoned unstarted node blocked on a cancelled sibling;
   - goal-attach.

   **Fix:** state a skip rule. Rules keyed on `outcomeEventId` / `unarchivedEventId` skip `NULL` (imported history), and 3b's terminal-child digest rail does the same. This replaces Area K's "stamp terminal children as notified".
3. **Restate Area K's import rules:** workstream rows are imported for non-archived threads only; `held` is 0 for done/cancelled rows; for `yielded`, `awaiting_orchestrator` is added to the copied attention set (a union, not a replacement).

## Nice-to-have

1. **`OrchestrationV2DomainEventJson` needs its own splice.** It is a separate hand-written union (`contracts/orchestrationV2.ts:2333`). The JSON event base (`:2320`) and the event base (`:1521`) are not exported. Typecheck will force this, but list it among the splices.
2. **One exhaustive-switch site is missing from the list.** `relay/AgentAwarenessRelay.ts:78–137` (`shouldPublishAgentAwarenessEvent`, explicit `boolean` return, no `default`) should return `false` for Loom events. Risk (2) also says "two known sites" while w1 lists five.
3. **The arm discards `cancelUnsettledEffects` from the nested `dispatchRunInterrupt`.** Upstream returns it for a run interrupted before its provider turn started (`:8231–8237`, consumed at `:9581`/`:9686`). Thread it through. Also, `dispatchRunInterrupt` rejects a run that is not interruptible (`:8057`), which would leave that descendant's cascade id receipted and dead. Skip the interrupt in that case rather than failing.
4. **Pin spawn's `creationSource` to `mcp` or `server`.** `isProviderNativeSubagentThread` (`contracts:442`) makes a subagent-lineage thread created with `creationSource: "provider"` read-only: `message.dispatch` is rejected at `Orchestrator.ts:9546–9555`.
5. **Tighten the `planReDrive` sketch.**
   - `cancelledDepEventId` is unbound.
   - The planner has no `now`, yet Loom commands require `createdAt`.
   - `gateLegFor`'s id scheme is unspecified; the strategy has one: `server:workstream-gate:<R>:<round>:<leg>`.
   - `composeGateLeg` does I/O inside a planner described as pure.
   - Every archived or cancelled row ever recorded is treated as a cascade root on every pass (quadratic over history), and the unarchive and archive cascades also catch descendants created *after* the episode. Bound both to descendants that existed at the episode stamp.
6. **The reactor's triggers omit terminal `run.updated`,** so a merge-back deferral is not retried until some unrelated event arrives, or until 3b's tick exists.
7. **Each blocked auto-settle attempt writes a rejected receipt and a warning, every sweep minute, per blocked thread.** Filter blocked threads in the settlement hunk (which needs the Loom read for M4 anyway) and keep the decider check as the race guard.
8. **Older and store-built mobile clients will break.** Loom event types in the per-thread client stream, and goal kinds in the shell stream, fail those clients' closed-union decoders. The web does not need Loom events, since it reads `shell.workstream`. Consider filtering Loom events out of the client thread stream.
9. **Shell payload size.** `LoomThreadShellFields` spreads the whole record (`notifySendLog`, `handoffDestinations`, the consult and peer summaries) onto every `thread.updated`. Trim it to what 3d renders.
10. **Small correctness and clutter notes.**
    - The `sqlite_master` guard on the renames is defensive clutter, given the tables exist on every database.
    - Arm and hunk reads through `LoomStoreV2` do not see events pending in the same command (upstream uses `getProjectionWithPendingEvents` for this); say so.
    - `activityRunStatus` is an optional field (`contracts:1747`), so test it with `!= null`.
    - The `quiescenceCandidate` predicate ignores `pendingBackgroundTasks`, which settlement treats as not idle.
11. **Gaps against the strategy.**
    - The started-dependents warning is emitted only on `gate.rework`; a parent's `outcome.set null` reopen gets none (strategy Area C lists it).
    - The `runtime-request.respond` live-waiter hunk's move to 3a is not stated under "Out".
    - The `continueThreadsAfterServerUpdate` default is global, not "for Loom".
12. **`t-lock`'s "ThreadCommandExecutor spans" do not exist.** `ThreadCommandExecutor.ts` is a bare `KeyedLock`. Specify a recording lock layer for the test. A related gap: concurrent `dependencies.set` on two siblings, each under its own lock, can create a cycle. Note it, or accept it.

## Where things stand

The work stays inside the gate: this report goes back to the planner as its rework brief. Nothing needs the parent orchestrator yet, except to note task `f78944f6` (Phase 4 import plan).

```ts
// packages/shared/src/workstreamStart.loom.ts
export interface StartNode { readonly id: ThreadId; readonly parentThreadId: ThreadId | null; readonly held: boolean;
  readonly outcome: "done" | "cancelled" | null; readonly kickoffAt: string | null; readonly kickoffBriefPath: string | null;
  readonly blockedBy: ReadonlyArray<ThreadId>; readonly archivedAt: string | null; readonly deletedAt: string | null; }

export const dependenciesSatisfied = (node: StartNode, byId: ReadonlyMap<ThreadId, StartNode>) =>
  node.blockedBy.every((id) => byId.get(id)?.outcome === "done");

  node.parentThreadId !== null && node.archivedAt === null && node.deletedAt === null &&
```

`loomTurnStartRules`, in order, for a thread with a sidecar:

1. **Reject permanently** when `workstream.deletedAt !== null` or `archivedAt !== null` — a message to a dead target fails once (its sender gets the error; a re-drive planner never produces one, §4).
2. **First-turn dependency gate.** If `parentThreadId !== null && kickoffAt === null && !dependenciesSatisfied(node, siblings)` → `OrchestratorDispatchError` naming the unsatisfied dependency (`describeUnsatisfiedDependency`). Applies to every path including a human send from the composer; the dispatcher's kickoff passes by construction.
3. **Held release by a human.** If `held && kickoffAt === null && command.createdBy === "user"` → emit `thread.held-set false` (acting on a held node is the release). A control-plane message to a held node (`loom.origin` set) is refused — the dispatcher never sends one, and a stale one must not start a held node.
4. **Attention clear.** If `command.createdBy === "user" || command.loom?.origin !== undefined`, and the stored attention set is non-empty → emit `thread.attention-cleared` (all). Upstream's own notification-source dispatches (PR-watch wake, a schedule fire) have neither and leave attention alone — a shipper's `awaiting_acceptance` survives a failing-check wake. A steer runs this too, on the *target* only: a child's yield steered into its parent clears nothing on the child.
5. **Kickoff stamp.** If `kickoffAt === null` → emit `thread.kickoff-recorded { kickoffAt: now, messageId, origin: command.loom?.origin ?? (command.createdBy === "user" ? "user" : "other") }`. The first turn by anyone is the start; the promotion rule then never fires for this thread again.
6. **Supersede** (slot reserved; implemented in Phase 3a with `runtime-request.create`): a `createdBy: user` message while a Loom-marked `user_input` request is pending resolves it as the tool result and withholds the turn start.

The `loom` field is carried onto the message record at the four construction sites (`...(command.loom === undefined ? {} : { loom: command.loom })`): the queued-run message (`Orchestrator.ts:~4874`), the immediate-start message (`:~5909`), the deferred/prepared path (`:~5217`) and the steer message in `dispatchSteerIntoRun` (`:~3765`, via its `input`). It lives on `OrchestrationV2ConversationMessage` only; the `user_message` turn item is untouched (decision log D8).

### Receipts

Loom's set-style commands that change nothing emit nothing and are **accepted with a receipt** — the hunk in `dispatchWithReceiptEffect` is one clause: `planned.events.length > 0 || command.type === "thread.background-work.settle" || isLoomCommand(command)`. Upstream already has the zero-event accepted-receipt path (it inserts the receipt at the thread's latest sequence); Loom reuses it. A re-driven `thread.outcome.set cancelled` on an already-cancelled descendant therefore records success, and a repeated raise of a standing reason costs no dispatcher pass.

`LoomDispatchDeferredError` is a `Schema.TaggedError` (`commandId`, `commandType`, `threadId`, `reason`) exported from `Orchestrator.loom.ts` and added to the `OrchestratorV2Error` union with one marked member. It is raised **only** when the same command can succeed later without anyone changing the target:

1. `start_if_idle` against a target with a blocking run (it goes idle).
2. A Loom gate leg (`thread.gate.rework` / `thread.gate.reverify`) whose nested `message.dispatch` would be queued behind a blocking run while the target has a pending merge-back transfer (`pendingMergeBackTransfersForThread(projection).length > 0`) — upstream rejects queued dispatch in that state ("queued merge-back consumption is not implemented yet"); the arm pre-checks and defers instead.

Everything permanently unsatisfiable is a receipted rejection that fails once: an archived or deleted target, a stale `routeEventId`, a cancelled thread, a dependency gate. The dispatcher (Phase 3b) treats `_tag === "LoomDispatchDeferredError"` as "try again next pass" and every other error as "this episode is dead — log it and surface it", which is the reviewer's confinement rule applied.

The clear runs when the message *starts or steers*: in `dispatchMessage` when the resolved mode is `steer_active` / `restart_active` or no blocking run exists, and otherwise in a marked hunk in `startNextQueuedRun` when the queued message it starts is user-authored or `orchestrator`-origin — so a human follow-up queued behind a running turn cannot erase a hold the agent raises at the end of that turn. A steer clears on the *target* only: a child's yield steered into its parent clears nothing on the child.
 5. **Kickoff stamp.** If `kickoffAt === null` → emit `thread.kickoff-recorded { kickoffAt: now, messageId, origin: command.loom?.origin ?? (command.createdBy === "user" ? "user" : "other") }`. The first turn by anyone is the start; the promotion rule then never fires for this thread again.
 6. **Supersede** (slot reserved; implemented in Phase 3a with `runtime-request.create`): a `createdBy: user` message while a Loom-marked `user_input` request is pending resolves it as the tool result and withholds the turn start.

It lives on `OrchestrationV2ConversationMessage` only; the `user_message` turn item is untouched (decision log D8).

 - **Human stop raises `needs_guidance`.** In the `run.interrupt` case, after upstream's `dispatchRunInterrupt`: `if (!command.commandId.startsWith("server:")) yield* loomHumanStopRaise(...)` — emits `thread.attention-raised needs_guidance` when the thread has a sidecar, `outcome === null`, and the reason is not already set. `workstream_stop` and cancel cascades use `server:` ids and raise nothing.
-- **Settle blockers.** In the `thread.auto-settle` case, before upstream's `dispatchThreadMutation`: `loomSettleBlockers(threadId)` rejects with `OrchestratorDispatchError` when the sidecar has `awaiting_orchestrator` in attention, or any live descendant (`listWorkstreamTree`) has `outcome === null` and `archivedAt === null`. The sweep uses a fresh `server:auto-settle:<thread>:<uuid>` id per attempt, so the receipted rejection costs nothing. Settle-on-merge goes through the same case. The **finished-root prompt settle** is a marked hunk in `ThreadSettlementService.resolveAutoSettlementAt`: when `thread.workstream?.outcome !== null && thread.workstream.parentThreadId === null`, the candidate settles at `outcomeAt` instead of after the inactivity window. Upstream's un-settle-on-any-dispatch stands (decision log D9).
+- **Settle blockers.** `ThreadSettlementService` loads its candidates from `projections.getSettlementCandidates` (a `ProjectionSettlementCandidate`, not the joined shell), so it reads `LoomStoreV2` directly — `LoomStore.layer` is added to its layer. Two marked hunks there: the candidate filter drops a thread whose sidecar has `awaiting_orchestrator` or a live descendant with `outcome === null && archivedAt === null` (so a blocked thread does not write a rejected receipt and a warning every sweep minute), and `resolveAutoSettlementAt` settles a **finished root** (`ws !== null && ws.outcome !== null && ws.parentThreadId === null`) at `outcomeAt` instead of after the inactivity window. The same blocker check sits in the `thread.auto-settle` decider case before upstream's `dispatchThreadMutation`, as the race guard for a candidate whose state changed after the sweep read it; the sweep uses a fresh `server:auto-settle:<thread>:<uuid>` id per attempt, so that rejection costs nothing. Settle-on-merge goes through the same case. Upstream's un-settle-on-any-dispatch stands (decision log D9).
 
 ### Receipts
 
 Loom's set-style commands that change nothing emit nothing and are **accepted with a receipt** — the hunk in `dispatchWithReceiptEffect` is one clause: `planned.events.length > 0 || command.type === "thread.background-work.settle" || isLoomCommand(command)`. Upstream already has the zero-event accepted-receipt path (it inserts the receipt at the thread's latest sequence); Loom reuses it. A re-driven `thread.outcome.set cancelled` on an already-cancelled descendant therefore records success, and a repeated raise of a standing reason costs no dispatcher pass.

### Restart recovery: what is continued, and what happens to held queued runs

Upstream has no "after reconciliation, before continuation" moment: `reconcileProjection` commits the reconciliation events **and** the `provider-runtime.continue` effect in one `commitCommand` (`ProviderRuntimeRecoveryService.ts:642–690`), with `enabled` decided per project from `continueThreadsAfterServerUpdate` before the call (`:741–745`), and `prepareForShutdown` enqueues the same effect at graceful shutdown (`:767–795`). The continuation itself is then an ordinary `message.dispatch` with `restartContinuationOfRunId` set (`RestartContinuation.ts:156–172`), and upstream already treats a stale continuation as an accepted no-op by emitting `thread.metadata-updated` (`Orchestrator.ts:~4385–4408`). Loom's policy therefore attaches at two real seams:

- **The "not continued" veto is rule 0 of `loomTurnStartRules`**: when `command.restartContinuationOfRunId !== undefined` and the sidecar says *not continued* (table below), emit upstream's no-op `thread.metadata-updated` and return — the continuation is accepted, receipted and does nothing, exactly as upstream handles a stale one. No hunk in the recovery service.
- **Held queued runs are released by a Loom startup pass** — `releaseHeldQueues` in `loomRecoveryPolicy.ts`, one marked call in `serverRuntimeStartup.ts` after upstream's reconciliation returns (beside Phase 1's foreign-home-guard line). It reads every Loom thread with a `queueHeld` run (`projectionStore.getThreadRecords(threadId, ["runs", "messages"])` for rows the store lists as Loom threads) and dispatches `queue.resume` or `queued-run.cancel` per the table, with `server:loom:recovery:<threadId>:<startupId>` ids.
- **The setting default is global**: `continueThreadsAfterServerUpdate` decodes to `true` for every thread in Loom's build (a marked default in `packages/contracts/src/settings.ts`), because the veto above is what keeps the no-silent-halt rules; upstream-only threads simply gain continuation.

<Table
  columns={["Loom thread state", "Continuation of the cut turn (rule 0)", "Held queued runs (startup pass)", "Why"]}
  rows={[
    ["No sidecar (an upstream-only thread)", "upstream's rule", "upstream's rule (held)", "Loom policy applies only to Loom threads"],
    ["outcome cancelled, or archived/deleted", "vetoed (no-op)", "queued-run.cancel each", "a dead thread does not wake"],
    ["stored attention contains needs_guidance or awaiting_acceptance, or a pending runtime request", "vetoed (no-op)", "stay held", "a human is already owed an action; their message is the release"],
    ["otherwise (a live Loom thread)", "continued with upstream's prompt (the steer stash rides it — driver item)", "queue.resume when any held queued run's message carries loom.origin", "a steered-tier wake that queued behind a preparing/starting target must not wait for a human; queue.resume is thread-wide and releases a human's queued follow-ups too, which is the correct reading of 'the thread is alive'"],
  ]}
/>

A cut **kickoff** needs no special row. A kickoff that was never accepted has no receipt and no `kickoffAt`, so the dispatcher's promotion fires it again on its next pass, verbatim. A kickoff that was accepted and queued is a held queued run released by the startup pass. A kickoff that was accepted and running is continued like any other cut turn — its text is already the first user message of the transcript, so "continue where you left off" is the right prompt.

### The one seam shared with the driver work item: the open-session field

Strategy Area G retains Loom's prompt composition and re-expresses its delivery as a Loom field on upstream's server-side `ProviderAdapterV2OpenSessionInput` (`orchestration-v2/ProviderAdapter.ts`; consumed by each adapter's `openSession`, e.g. `Adapters/ClaudeAdapterV2.ts:2988`), which `buildPiRpcLaunch` turns into `--append-system-prompt`, `--skill` and the second `--extension`:

```ts
// loom: on ProviderAdapterV2OpenSessionInput (owned by the driver work item)
loom?: {
  appendSystemPrompt: string;            // identity clause · role overlay · ship policy · role catalogue · goal context · relocation clause
  skills: ReadonlyArray<string>;         // repeated --skill paths from the role overlay
  extensions: ReadonlyArray<string>;     // Loom's extension beside upstream's bridge
  forkFrom?: { threadId: ThreadId; identityPath: string }; // launch-identity sidecar to replay argv verbatim
};
```

The field, the `ProviderSessionManager` composition hook that fills it and the launch-identity sidecar belong to the driver work item. What the substrate provides, and all it provides, are the reads the hook consumes: `LoomStoreV2.getWorkstream(threadId)` (role, goalId, anchorTaskId, forkFromThreadId, continuesThreadId), `goals.get(goalId)` and `tasks.listByGoal(goalId)`. The driver plan can be written against those three signatures without waiting on anything here.

 ## 4. Projection, sidecar tables and the re-drive planner
 
 ### The projector

One marked hunk at the top of `ProjectionStore.apply` folds Loom events in the same SQL transaction as upstream's projection writes and the receipt, so a tool handler that dispatches then reads sees its own write:

```ts
// apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProjectionStore.ts — inside apply()
// loom: sidecar tables are written in the commit transaction, beside upstream's projection
yield* applyLoomProjectionEvent(sql, event);
switch (event.type) { /* upstream, unchanged */ }
```

`applyLoomProjectionEvent(sql, event)` (`apps/server/src/loom/projection/loomProjection.ts`) is a plain function over the `SqlClient` already in scope — no new layer in the event sink. For a Loom event it runs the table effect from the §1 event table; for `thread.archived | unarchived | deleted | metadata-updated` it mirrors into `loom_thread_workstream` when a row exists and runs the goal cascades against `loom_goals`; for everything else it returns at once. Loom events fall out of upstream's switch unmatched and reach the trailing "bump `thread.updatedAt`" block, which is wanted: an attention raise or an outcome is activity. The in-memory `applyToProjection` gets a one-line `default: return base;` because the widened union makes its return non-exhaustive; the memory projection store never sees Loom tables and no Phase 2 test uses it.

### The shell join

`joinLoomShellFields(loomStore)(snapshot)` attaches `workstream` to each shell for which a row exists; threads without one carry no key. Two marked hunks in `Orchestrator.ts`'s service record wrap `getShellSnapshot` and `getThreadShell` so every consumer — ws, MCP, settlement, PR services — reads the joined shape. The web (3d) reads `shell.workstream.*`; nothing else on the shell changes.

### Goals: tables, idempotency, broadcast

Goals and tasks are **plain tables written by the Phase 3a tool handlers** through `LoomStoreV2.goals` / `.tasks`. Idempotency needs no ledger: ids are derived from the command id the MCP layer already stabilises per `clientRequestId` (`goalId = GoalId.make("goal:" + hash(commandId))`, `taskId` likewise), and every write is an upsert, so a retried `goal_task_add` lands on the same `task_id` and `goal_tasks_rewrite` is idempotent by construction (the submitted list *is* the tree). The 300-character register cap, round-trip identity and anchor scoping stay in the ported `goalTaskTree.ts` / `goalTaskMarkdown.ts` / `goalTaskAnchor.loom.ts` (3a brings them out of quarantine; their logic is engine-free).

Broadcast: `LoomGoalBroadcast` is a `PubSub<LoomGoalShellStreamItem>`; a handler publishes `goal.updated` / `goal.removed` after its write, and a small reactor on `streamDomainEvents` publishes after a projector-folded cascade (`thread.archived | unarchived | metadata-updated` on a thread whose sidecar names a goal). Each item carries `sequence` = `applicationEvents.latestApplicationSequence` at publish, so the client's cursor logic keys it like any other shell item. Because these items sit outside V2's event sequence, a client resuming from a cursor cannot catch up on goals from the cursor alone: `loadSnapshot` in `ws.ts` includes `goals` (one marked hunk) and Loom's connect-gap-aware subscriptions (3d) refetch the snapshot on reconnect. Contract hunks: two members on `OrchestrationV2ShellStreamItem`, `goals: Schema.optional(Schema.Array(LoomGoalShell))` on `OrchestrationV2ShellSnapshot`.

### The re-drive planner

Multi-thread effects become per-thread commands. `apps/server/src/loom/orchestration/redrive.ts`:

```ts
/** One episode-keyed command per affected thread. Pure over a graph snapshot. */
export const planReDrive = (rows: ReadonlyArray<LoomThreadWorkstream>): ReadonlyArray<OrchestrationV2ServerCommand> => [
  // cancel cascade: root cancelled → every live descendant with outcome null
  ...rows.filter((r) => r.outcome === "cancelled").flatMap((root) =>
    descendants(rows, root.threadId).filter((d) => d.outcome === null && d.deletedAt === null)
      .map((d) => outcomeSet(d.threadId, "cancelled", `server:loom:cascade-cancel:${root.outcomeEventId}:${d.threadId}`))),
  // wedged dependents: a live, unstarted node blocked on a cancelled same-parent sibling
  ...rows.filter((r) => r.outcome === null && r.kickoffAt === null && !r.attention.includes("needs_guidance"))
    .filter((r) => r.blockedBy.some((id) => cancelledSibling(rows, r, id)))
    .map((r) => attentionRaise(r.threadId, "needs_guidance", `server:loom:wedged:${cancelledDepEventId}:${r.threadId}`)),
  // archive / delete cascades keyed on the root's stamp; unarchive keyed on its event id
  ...rows.filter((r) => r.archivedAt !== null).flatMap((root) => descendants(rows, root.threadId)
    .filter((d) => d.archivedAt === null).map((d) => upstreamArchive(d.threadId, `server:loom:cascade-archive:${root.threadId}:${root.archivedAt}:${d.threadId}`))),
  ...rows.filter((r) => r.unarchivedEventId !== null && r.archivedAt === null).flatMap((root) => descendants(rows, root.threadId)
    .filter((d) => d.archivedAt !== null).map((d) => upstreamUnarchive(d.threadId, `server:loom:cascade-unarchive:${root.unarchivedEventId}:${d.threadId}`))),
  ...rows.filter((r) => r.deletedAt !== null).flatMap((root) => descendants(rows, root.threadId)
    .filter((d) => d.deletedAt === null).map((d) => upstreamDelete(d.threadId, `server:loom:cascade-delete:${root.threadId}:${root.deletedAt}:${d.threadId}`))),
  // goal attach down: a child with no goal whose parent has one
  ...rows.filter((r) => r.goalId === null && parentOf(rows, r)?.goalId).map((r) => goalSet(r.threadId, parentOf(rows, r)!.goalId, `server:loom:goal-attach:${r.threadId}:${parentOf(rows, r)!.goalId}`)),
  // gate legs from the latest route on a source (loop → rework on the target; loop-back → reverify on the source; resolve → resolve on the counterpart)
  ...rows.filter((r) => r.lastRoute !== null).map((r) => gateLegFor(r, rows)),
];
```

`runReDrivePass(orchestrator, commandReceipts, loomStore)` reads `listActiveWorkstreams()` (plus archived rows for the cascades), plans, skips any command whose id already has a receipt (`commandReceipts.getByCommandId`), dispatches the rest **sequentially** (one lock at a time, never nested), and classifies results: accepted → done; `LoomDispatchDeferredError` → leave for the next pass; any other error → log at warning with the episode key (the episode is receipted dead; Phase 3b's advisory rail surfaces it). The gate-leg text and `controlPayload` come from a `composeGateLeg` the dispatcher owns in 3b; Phase 2 ships it with a minimal fixed template so the test can run, marked for 3b to replace.

`LoomReDriveReactor` subscribes to `streamDomainEvents`, debounces on `thread.outcome-set | thread.route-taken | thread.archived | thread.unarchived | thread.deleted | thread.goal-set`, runs the pass, and runs once at startup. Phase 3b folds it into the dispatcher's pass (first rails, before promotion) and owns the periodic tick; until then the reactor is what keeps cascades and gates moving in the Phase 2 smoke.

The window the strategy accepted is visible here: between a reviewer's `route-taken` and the coder's `gate-rework-accepted` the board reads the coder as done for one pass; dependents cannot start in that window because `isMemberOfUnresolvedGate` (the reviewer is non-terminal and carries the loop route) already holds them, and the promotion predicate excludes gate members.

## 5. Migrations

Three entries appended to `loomMigrationEntries`, run by the existing `runAllMigrations()` from `Sqlite.ts`'s `setup` — upstream's `Migrations.ts` untouched. The copy to `statev2.sqlite` carries `loom_sql_migrations` at `1045`, so on a copied database exactly these three run; on a fresh install `1001`–`1048` run after upstream's `1`–`56`.

```sql
-- 1046_LoomThreadWorkstream.ts
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS loom_thread_workstream (
  thread_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  project_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  goal_id TEXT, anchor_task_id TEXT,
  parent_thread_id TEXT, root_thread_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  role TEXT, purpose TEXT, graph_key TEXT, kickoff_brief_path TEXT,
  held INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, held_since TEXT,
  outcome TEXT, outcome_at TEXT, outcome_event_id TEXT,
  kickoff_at TEXT,
  attention TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  blocked_by TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', dependencies_since TEXT,
  spawn_generation TEXT, fork_from_thread_id TEXT, continues_thread_id TEXT,
  routes TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', gate_rounds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, pending_rework INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_outcome TEXT, last_route TEXT,
  report_path TEXT,
  handoff_destinations TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', notify_send_log TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  archived_at TEXT, unarchived_event_id TEXT, deleted_at TEXT,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_loom_ws_parent ON loom_thread_workstream(parent_thread_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_loom_ws_root ON loom_thread_workstream(root_thread_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_loom_ws_goal ON loom_thread_workstream(goal_id);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_loom_ws_graph_key ON loom_thread_workstream(parent_thread_id, graph_key) WHERE graph_key IS NOT NULL;

-- 1047_LoomGoalTables.ts (data travels with the rename; SQLite rewrites the FK reference)
ALTER TABLE projection_goals RENAME TO loom_goals;
ALTER TABLE projection_goal_tasks RENAME TO loom_goal_tasks;

-- 1048_LoomConsultAndPeerMessageTables.ts
```

The renames are guarded with `IF EXISTS` semantics via a `sqlite_master` check (the V1 tables exist on every database `1003`/`1016`/`1032` ran on, which is all of them). Heartbeats, the usage ledger and the thread-search index get their `loom_*` migrations in the phase that writes them (3b, 3c); Phase 2 creates only what its projector and the 3a handlers write.

**Import expressibility (Phase 4).** Every V1 fact the strategy maps has a column: `planned → held 1`; `ready / in_progress → held 0, outcome NULL`; `yielded → outcome NULL + attention ['awaiting_orchestrator']`; `done / cancelled → outcome`; `kickoff_at` = the first user-turn time from the copied `projection_turns` (import time if absent) for any thread with a turn; `root_thread_id` from the parent chain; stored attention copies as is; `last_outcome` with a synthetic `eventId` and `report_path` copy across; `blocked_by`, `routes`, `gate_rounds`, `pending_rework`, `spawn_generation`, `fork_from_thread_id`, `continues_thread_id`, `anchor_task_id`, `graph_key`, `kickoff_brief_path`, `handoff_destinations`, `notify_send_log` are one-to-one. Goals, tasks, consults and peer messages need no import at all (renamed in place, thread ids preserved by upstream's importer). The importer writes rows directly — `thread.workstream-created` is never emitted for imported threads, so no Loom event exists for them and no episode-keyed rail fires. Session binding is upstream's `provider-thread.updated` with a strong `nativeThreadRef` (the shape `dispatchThreadCreate` writes for `importedNativeThread`); nothing in this schema constrains it.

## 6. Quiescence as completion — the substrate half

The semantic: a started child that goes quiet without `workstream_submit` is treated as having yielded, not as owing a human. Phase 2 provides the state and the predicate; Phase 3b's rail writes the report and dispatches the synthesised submit.

- **The event and the state.** The dispatcher dispatches `thread.work.submit { threadId, reportPath, outcome: "quiescent" }` with a `server:loom:quiescent:<threadId>:<lastRunId>` id. The arm accepts `quiescent` only on `server:` ids, records `thread.outcome-recorded { outcome: "quiescent", decision: "yield", synthesised: true }` and raises `awaiting_orchestrator`. `routeWorkSubmit` returns `yield` for it before the rework interception (§2), so a gate member that goes quiet also yields and never resolves or loops its gate. Spawn and scaffold refuse `quiescent` in any route's `on` list.
- **The hook.** V2 run completion as projected: Phase 3b subscribes to `run.updated` with a terminal status on `streamDomainEvents` and re-evaluates on the periodic tick; it never listens to the adapter's `agent_settled`.
